summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and prior port infections was admitted for persistent fevers, chills, and pelvic pain radiating to her thighs following a course of antibiotics for a presumed UTI. Blood cultures from an outside hospital grew Bacillus species. Initial imaging showed no fistula or bowel obstruction but revealed splenomegaly and a new lung nodule. A pelvic MRI identified a small abscess in the right pectineus muscle, determined to be the source of bacteremia. She was treated with IV vancomycin, completed a course of antibiotics, and became afebrile. Her pain was managed with IV then oral analgesics, and she received IV iron for iron deficiency anemia. Her anticoagulation for SVC syndrome required careful management due to variable coumadin absorption, including a brief bridge with fondaparinux. She had a minor fall with no fracture. She was discharged home on a short course of IV antibiotics, a dilaudid taper, and close follow-up for repeat imaging and blood cultures.
problems: Anticoagulation management in setting of short bowel syndrome
